chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Muḥammad ibn Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, he said:

I said to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: May a man perform the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ at al-Mawqif? He said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم had indeed done that; he performed them both in the mountain pass.

Thus, the correct way regarding this report is that it is to be understood as applying to one whom some impediment prevents from coming to Jamʿ until it becomes quite late in the evening. But when there is choice, that is not permissible in any circumstance. And that which indicates that what is intended is what we have mentioned...

key_terms.الِاخْتِيَارِ: having choice and no constraining excuse

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ at ʿArafāt on the night of al-Naḥr?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of performing Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ at ʿArafāt on the night of al-Naḥr. Although the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم is reported to have done so in a particular circumstance, the report is understood to apply only where an impediment delays a person from reaching Jamʿ; otherwise, doing so by choice is not permitted.
